short: Lip-reader text conditioning (M07) is new but standard: words come from the lip reader (19.1% reading WER becomes 21.4%; 86.2% unguided), and no cascade control is run.
position: LipVoicer [@yemini2024lipvoicer] changes three components: lip-reader text steers synthesis at use time (M07), a CTC recognizer trained on noised mel-spectrograms carries all text supervision (M02), and a video-conditioned diffusion model generates the mel-spectrogram (M06). The authors' claim (Sec. 1) to be the first to condition a video-to-speech synthesizer on lip-reader text holds against 165 ledger studies (Appendix), with [@hegde2023towards] [concurrent]. M07 is still standard: lip-to-text plus TTS already used such text [@hegde2022arbitrary], and no gain over it is shown. The words come from the lip reader, not the synthesizer: on LRS3 output WER is 21.4% against the lip reader's 19.1%, 5.4% with ground-truth text, and 86.2% without guidance, worse than the Lip2Speech baseline at 57.4% (Tables 4, 6, 7). No baseline received that text, so "state-of-the-art results" (Sec. 1) pit a 2023 lip reader against text-free synthesizers. M02, M06 and M12 are standard; the main tables score words with an ASR from the same work as the lip reader.
